name: gear-armor
prompt:
Use the image generation tool. Make ONE square 1024x1024 PNG: a production pixel-art cutout sheet of wearable ARMOR and BACK pieces for a Spine skeletal rig of the SAME wuxia heroine shown in the references.

Reference 1 is the existing part sheet: match its exact pixel-art look (hard-edged 16-bit pixel art, chunky square pixels about 4 output pixels wide, limited palette, 1-2 pixel dark brown outline, soft pixel shading from top-right light, no antialiasing, no gradients, no blur). Reference 2 is the heroine's sleeveless TORSO part (neck to tunic hem, facing right in three-quarter side view): every body-worn piece below must be drawn at the SAME pixel scale and to FIT ON THAT TORSO, same 3/4 view facing right. Reference 3 is the full character for identity.

Background: flat solid pure magenta #FF00FF everywhere, no checkerboard, no shadow, no text, no grid lines. Arrange as an invisible 3 by 3 grid, one fully isolated piece centered in each cell with generous magenta padding. Pieces never touch each other.

Row 1:
1. Wuxia LAMELLAR chest armor (zhajia) worn over the tunic: small overlapping steel scales laced with dark red cord in horizontal rows, dark leather border and shoulder straps, a round bronze protective mirror (huxinjing) on the chest. Shaped like a real vest covering chest and belly, open at the neck and armholes, slightly curved to follow the torso in 3/4 view. Same width as the torso reference, height from collarbone to waist sash. No arms, no head.
2. IRON shoulder guard (pauldron) for one shoulder: three overlapping curved steel plates getting wider downward, riveted gold trim, a leather strap at the top, seen from the side, hanging straight down. About as wide as the torso's shoulder.
3. LEATHER shoulder guard: same shape and size as piece 2 but layered brown hardened leather with stitched edges.
Row 2:
4. Long CRIMSON CAPE hanging from the back of the neck, seen from the right side as it would look behind a character facing right: fastened at the top with a small gold clasp, falling down behind the body to knee level, hem sweeping back to the LEFT, natural cloth folds, gold embroidered hem. Height about 1.8 times the torso reference.
5. The SAME cape in deep midnight blue with silver hem.
6. Wuxia bronze HAIR CROWN (guan) that sits on top of a hair bun, small, with a gold hairpin passing through it horizontally, red jewel.
Row 3:
7. Conical bamboo STRAW HAT (douli) seen from the side at slight angle, woven texture, a red chin cord hanging, width about 2.2 times the head.
8. Brown calabash WINE GOURD with a red cord and knot at the top, small, hanging.
9. Green JADE PENDANT disc (bi) with a red tassel hanging below, small.

Keep pixel art crisp and consistent with reference 1. These are clothing and props for animation cutouts.

name: outfit-robe
prompt:

Reference 1 is the existing part sheet (4x4 grid): row 1 has the torso, row 2 has four arm sleeves (rear upper arm, front upper arm, rear forearm with open palm, front forearm with open palm, all pointing straight DOWN with round joint caps). Reference 2 is the torso part alone. Match the exact pixel-art look (hard-edged 16-bit pixel art, chunky square pixels about 4 output pixels wide, limited palette, 1-2 pixel dark brown outline, no antialiasing, no gradients).

CRITICAL: every new torso must have EXACTLY the same silhouette, size, pose and proportions as reference 2 (same neck position, same shoulder line, same waist sash height, same hem length, facing right in three-quarter side view) so it can replace it on the skeleton. Only the clothing design and colors change. Keep the neck skin stub at the top like the reference.

Background: flat solid pure magenta #FF00FF, no checkerboard, no shadow, no text, no grid lines. Invisible 4 by 3 grid (4 columns, 3 rows), one fully isolated piece centered in each cell, generous padding, pieces never touch.

Row 1: four sleeveless TORSOS, no head, arms or legs:
 1. black and crimson swordswoman robe with high collar and gold buttons, crimson sash;
 2. white and gold scholar-knight robe with gold cloud embroidery, gold sash;

Row 3: matching FOREARM sleeves with bare OPEN PALM for torsos 1 and 2 (rear then front for each), elbow at top, fingertips at bottom, pointing straight down, same size as reference 1 row 2 forearms, including the wrist cuff in the new outfit colors.

Keep pixel art crisp and consistent with reference 1. Clothing only, no gore.

hat-straw

name: pants2
hands
prompt:
Use the image generation tool. Make ONE PNG, 1536 wide by 1024 tall: new HAND parts for a Spine skeletal rig of the SAME wuxia heroine.

Reference 1 shows the current FOREARM with an OPEN PALM (left) and the forearm with a FIST (right). The open palm looks like a flat paddle: fingers merged into one block and no visible thumb. Reference 2 is the full part sheet, reference 3 the character, for style and pixel scale. Match the exact pixel-art look (hard-edged 16-bit pixel art, chunky square pixels about 4 output pixels wide, limited palette, warm skin tones like the reference, 1-2 pixel dark brown outline, no antialiasing, no gradients).

Draw ONLY the HAND (no forearm, no sleeve, no cuff), starting at the wrist. Every hand hangs STRAIGHT DOWN like the reference palm: wrist at the TOP, fingers toward the bottom, seen from the side as on a character facing RIGHT, about the same size as the reference hand. Each hand includes a small round wrist stub at the top that will tuck under the sleeve cuff.

Row 1, three hands (for the near side of the body, the back of the hand facing the viewer):
1. OPEN PALM: a natural open hand, fingers together and slightly curved, the THUMB clearly separated and visible, knuckle creases, elegant and readable;
2. RELAXED hand for walking: fingers loosely curled, thumb resting along the index finger, calm and natural;
3. PALM STRIKE hand: the wrist bent back so the fingers point toward the RIGHT (forward) while the heel of the palm pushes DOWN, fingers together, thumb tucked, like a kung fu palm strike.
Row 2: the same three hands again, identical design.

Layout on flat solid pure magenta #FF00FF, no grid lines, no text: 3 columns by 2 rows, every hand fully isolated with generous padding.

name: palm-strike
prompt:
Use the image generation tool. Make ONE PNG, 1536 wide by 1024 tall: a kung fu PALM STRIKE hand (li zhang, standing palm) for a pixel-art wuxia heroine facing RIGHT.

Reference 1 is her new open hand part (skin tone, outline, pixel scale). Reference 2 is her FOREARM with sleeve cuff lying HORIZONTAL, elbow on the left, wrist on the right. Reference 3 is the character, reference 4 the part sheet, for style. Match the exact pixel-art look (hard-edged 16-bit pixel art, chunky square pixels about 4 output pixels wide, warm skin tones, 1-2 pixel dark brown outline, no antialiasing, no gradients).

Draw ONLY the HAND as it looks at the end of a horizontal forearm that comes in from the LEFT: the wrist is at the LEFT edge of the hand, at mid height. The wrist is bent back 90 degrees so the fingers point straight UP, fingers held together and straight, the thumb tucked along the side of the palm, the PALM faces RIGHT (forward, toward the enemy) and the heel of the palm is the part that pushes forward. We see the hand from the side, the little-finger edge nearest to us. It must look like a clean, strong, readable palm strike, anatomically correct, about the same size as reference 1. Include a small wrist stub at the left that tucks under the sleeve cuff. No forearm, no sleeve, no cuff.

Draw FOUR variants of this same pose (slightly different finger shaping and thumb placement) so the best can be chosen, in a row, each fully isolated with generous padding.
Background: flat solid pure magenta #FF00FF, no grid lines, no text.

name: face-phoenix
prompt:
Use the image generation tool. Make ONE PNG, 1536 wide by 1024 tall: FIVE HEAD parts of the SAME wuxia heroine with a NEW FACE, one per hair color.

Reference 1 (left piece) is her original HEAD part: facing RIGHT in 3/4 side view, brown hair with bangs, side locks and a bun with a red hair tie. Reference 2 shows the same head in four other hair colors (row 1). Reference 3 is the part sheet for style. Match the exact pixel-art look (hard-edged 16-bit pixel art, chunky square pixels about 4 output pixels wide, warm East Asian skin tones, 1-2 pixel dark brown outline, no antialiasing, no gradients).

CRITICAL: the HAIR must stay exactly the same as the references (same hairstyle, bangs, side locks, bun, red tie, same colors), same head size, same pose and angle, same neck. ONLY the FACE changes: PHOENIX EYES: long narrow upswept almond eyes with sharp outer corners and a thin eyeliner flick, straight elegant brows, a slim V-shaped jaw, small calm mouth. Cool and sharp swordswoman. The face must stay East Asian and appealing, drawn clean and readable at this small pixel size.

Five heads, all with this same new face, hair colors in this order: 1 brown (like reference 1), 2 jet black, 3 silver-white, 4 auburn red-brown, 5 dark chestnut with one white streak (colors exactly like reference 2).
Layout: row 1 has heads 1, 2, 3; row 2 has heads 4, 5. Every head fully isolated with generous padding, no ponytail, no body.
Background: flat solid pure magenta #FF00FF, no grid lines, no text.
